topic.title: Commit Changes
topic.shortdesc: Commit staged files to the local repository and configure commit options.

body.p: After you stage the files that you want to include, enter a commit message in the Commit message area and commit the files to your local repository. You can also reuse a previous commit message.

The toolbar above the Commit message area includes options that affect the commit:
Amend last commit - Modifies the most recent commit. Use this option to combine staged changes with the previous commit instead of creating a new commit. You can also edit the previous commit message without changing its snapshot. Do not use this action on public commits, which are commits that were pushed to the remote repository.
Automatically push changes to remote when committing - Pushes the committed changes to the remote repository after the commit is performed.

ul.li: If your environment is configured for commit signing, you can sign commits using SSH or GPG keys.

GPG support in JGit, the Java library used for Git operations, honors the GNUPGHOME environment variable. If this variable is set to a valid directory path, that directory is used as the GPG home directory where the keys are stored. If GNUPGHOME is not set, JGit defaults to %APPDATA%\gnupg on Windows and ~/.gnupg on other operating systems. Alternatively, you can set the jgit.gpg.home Java system property, which takes precedence over GNUPGHOME if both are set.
